To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The energy cost of cryptographic operations is not negligible, (2) the communication cost is not negligible, and (3) the security level of the application has an impact on the energy cost.

(i) the energy consumption of cryptographic primitives is in the same range as the communication energy cost, (ii) the energy cost of wireless communications depends on the wireless technology, (iii) authentication schemes for RFID have a large energy cost and are thus not suitable for low-cost RFID systems, and (iv) the energy cost for secure wireless communications can be reduced significantly by using lightweight cryptographic algorithms and protocols

the energy cost of secure communications is dominated by the communication cost and the cryptographic primitives, and that the energy cost is highly dependent on the wireless standard and the security requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (i) the energy cost of wireless standards; (ii) the energy cost for different security and privacy applications; (iii) the energy cost in different wireless devices; (iv) the energy cost and security/privacy of cryptographic primitives.
the energy consumption of wireless security and privacy applications, and how this affects the design of secure protocols and cryptographic primitives.
the energy cost of security and privacy solutions, in the context of wireless communications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
energy efficiency is a major factor to take into account when developing security protocols for wireless networks.
energy efficiency is not a sufficient criterion for security and privacy, but a necessary condition.

energy is a crucial factor in the security and privacy of wireless networks, and the energy cost of secure communication should be considered as early as possible in the design phase of the wireless application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy cost for secure wireless communications can vary from a few microjoules to a few milli-joules.
the energy cost is not only a matter of the cryptographic algorithms, but also of the communication protocols.
the energy cost for wireless security is a tradeoff between security and performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy cost of wireless communications is not negligible, and that energy efficiency is a key factor in the design and deployment of wireless security solutions.
the security and privacy requirements for wireless applications should be carefully defined, in order to achieve an efficient energy budget for secure and private wireless communications.
energy efficiency and security/privacy are not necessarily conflicting goals.
